newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican crude port Dos Bocas open, Pajaritos shut.
newsitem.headline: Mexican crude port Dos Bocas open, Pajaritos shut.

text.p: Mexican crude port Dos Bocas reopened at 0800 local/1300 GMT on Wednesday as storms in the region relaxed, while Pajaritos port remained shut, port officials said.
The two ports were closed since late on Saturday because of a cold front in the Gulf of Mexico.

Pajaritos remained shut with winds between 45 and 55 km per hour and waves eight to 10 feet high. Port authorities said they will be periodically reviewing weather conditions at the terminal and said operations could resume later in the day.

Renewed operations at Dos Bocas will gradually make up for the lag in shipping, an official said, with at least two ships waiting to load contracted Maya heavy crude from state oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex).
U.S.-bound John Young was waiting for a contracted 1.45 million barrels, and U.S. Bona Spring was waiting to load 525,000 barrels..
Pajaritos shipped an average 416,200 barrels per day (bpd) of crude in 1996, Dos Bocas shipped about 505,900 bpd and Cayo Arcas shipped 576,300 bpd, according to the latest figures from Pemex.
